findings.governingReading: 重荷 centers his self-accusation as weight she must carry because of the contract.
findings.explanation: Shirou calling himself Saber's greatest burden becomes calling himself her greatest weakness.

findings.governingReading: 不可能かもしれない presents impossibility as a possibility within her escalating assessment.
findings.explanation: Saber says cornering Berserker may be impossible, but English says it is likely impossible.

findings.highlight: nullified Rin's magecraft with his own brute strength.
findings.evidenceJa: 肉体の強度のみで凛の魔術を無効化した
findings.governingReading: 肉体の強度 names the body's hardness or structural toughness as the defensive basis.
findings.explanation: Berserker nullifying Rin's magecraft through bodily durability becomes doing so through brute strength.

findings.evidenceJa: 宝具ってのは強力な武器なんだろ？
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks generally whether Noble Phantasms are powerful weapons.
findings.explanation: A plural predicate is paired with singular ‘Noble Phantasm.’

findings.highlight: Anti-Fortress Noble Phantasms wipe out massive areas in a single blow.
findings.evidenceJa: 一撃で全てを決する対城宝具。
findings.governingReading: 一撃で全てを決する describes decisive battle scale without directly defining the effect as area destruction.
findings.explanation: An Anti-Fortress Noble Phantasm deciding everything in one blow becomes wiping out massive areas.

findings.highlight: Anti-army and Anti-Fortress attacks, just from their names, sounds like giant missiles.
findings.evidenceJa: 対軍やら対城やら、そんなミサイルみたいな攻撃
findings.governingReading: Shirou compares the named attack classes to missiles.
findings.explanation: The plural subject ‘attacks’ takes the singular verb ‘sounds.’
